DEP-app is an experimental project app that tries to detect earthquake shaking using the phone accelerometer and gyroscope.

How it works

1) Gravity removal: the phone measures acceleration about 50 times per second. A low-pass filter removes gravity, leaving only vibration.

2) STA/LTA: the average vibration of the last 0.5 s (STA) is compared with the last 10 s (LTA). A sudden jump in the ratio means shaking has started. Seismologists use this classic method to pick earthquake waves.

3) Gyroscope check: if the phone is rotating (held, in a pocket, carried) the motion comes from a person, so detection pauses.

4) Duration and continuity: earthquakes shake continuously for seconds, while door slams and footsteps die out quickly. Shaking must therefore last at least 1-2 seconds.

5) Estimated intensity: the Mercalli intensity is estimated from peak acceleration using Wald et al. (1999).

Each event is saved as a CSV file (Android/data/io.github.mustafaadsiz135.depapp/files/kayitlar).

IMPORTANT: this is not an official early-warning system. It only detects shaking where the phone is and cannot warn before shaking starts. Follow your official earthquake authority for information.
